messages:
Jess (AE): Heads-up — Orion Health wants a perf run that mirrors their private deployment with customer-managed KMS + TLS termination in front. They suspect encryption will add latency (20-30ms). Can we validate with a smoke POC next Tue? cc @Nadia :eyes:
Nadia (Solutions Eng): Yes. Proposed plan: spin a dedicated pool in us-east-1, enable mTLS + HSM envelope keys, model redwood-v2-large. Test matrix: warmup 5k reqs, 10m run with 200 QPS sustained, 10m ramp down. Capture p50/p95/p99, token breakdown, and error traces. Also run fp16 vs int8 quantized.
Tara (ML Eng): Note on workload: use seq_len=512 and realistic prompt distribution (we have the clinical prompt set from Orion). Test both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. KV cache should be enabled — include a cold vs warmed cache variation.
Mike (SRE): I can provision isolated pool and firewall rules. Need customer IP CIDRs and their KMS public cert. Example runbook snippet I’ll use to deploy:
```
helm upgrade --install redwood-test ./charts/dedicated 
  --set model.name=redwood-v2-large 
  --set tls.enabled=true 
  --set kms.provider=hsm 
  --set autoscale.min=2 --set autoscale.max=8
```
Ping me the certs and IPs.
Lee (Orion Health): We can provide certs and CIDRs today. Our SLAs: for interactive clinical flows we need p95 < 350ms at seq=512. For async batch it's fine up to p99=500ms. Can you confirm both modes?
Nadia (Solutions Eng): Quick expectations: HSM unwrap per-call is expensive (~5-8ms) if done every request. We’ll use envelope keys with a cached host key by default — that should be ~1-2ms overhead. We'll run both: (A) HSM per-request; (B) envelope cached key.
deploy-bot: deploy started: redwood/dedicated/test-pool @1799994330
Mike (SRE): Run finished (initial smoke). Summary: model=redwood-v2-large, config=kms=envelope-cache+tls, seq=512, qps=200, duration=10m. Results:
``
- p50: 78ms
- p95: 215ms
- p99: 420ms
- error_rate: 0.2% (transient timeouts during GC)
- token-cost delta vs no-encryption: +0.8 tokens/req CPU time equivalent
```
Nadia (Solutions Eng): p95 looks good, p99 spikes are high. Investigation: a few hosts hit GC and there were minor HSM latency spikes in the per-request test we ran earlier. Next steps: enable aggressive prefix warming, bump pool size to reduce variability, and run int8 quantized test.
Jess (AE): Thanks team — I'll update Lee. Also flag for pricing: HSM envelope operations will impact cost model for Private — finance calc suggests ~\$0.12/request if we do per-request HSM; with cached envelope keys cost is negligible. Can finance confirm for dedicated/private pricing? cc @Finance
Lee (Orion Health): That aligns with our expectations. For clinical synchronous flow we need p95<350ms; p99 up to 500ms acceptable for async. Please try int8 + cached keys and re-run. Thu 14:00 ET works for us.
Nadia (Solutions Eng): Scheduled: Thu 14:00 ET. I'll post the test matrix, exact CLI commands, and the dataset link in this thread before the run. Will also share flamegraphs if we still see p99 spikes.
Mike (SRE): I'll add more nodes to the pool and enable node pinning to avoid GC overlap. Will collect per-host metrics + HSM latency traces.
Jess (AE): Great — I'll confirm with the customer and include the pricing note. Thanks all :thumbsup:
